title: OrcaSlicer and Practical Print Impact
summary: Which Orca presets change, what stays filament calibration, and what prints should feel like after migration.

content.text: Plain summary

Yes, the firmware work changes the required Orca setup for the mainline candidate. Orca should no longer own homing, meshing, factory wipes, bed calibration, or final parking. It emits object labels, calls the reviewed lifecycle macros, and stores measured pressure advance in each filament profile.
Required profile contract
Use the repository's audited machine profile, calibration-required filament profiles, and review-only process profiles. The default machine is T300 AUDITED Runtime 0.4 - REVIEW ONLY.
G-code flavor must be Klipper.
Object labels and exclude-object output must be enabled so EXCLUDE_OBJECT_DEFINE records appear before START_PRINT.
Print sequence must be by layer, not by object.
Machine start G-code must be only START_PRINT BED_TEMP=... EXTRUDER_TEMP=....
Machine end G-code must be END_PRINT.
Pause and filament change should call PAUSE and M600.
Per-layer timelapse may use TIMELAPSE_TAKE_FRAME in Orca before-layer-change G-code.
New-project default

This laptop now has all eight reviewed T300 Orca 2.4.2 presets installed, with the zero-hop audited runtime machine selected as the default for new projects. The repository installer supports Linux, Windows, and macOS and makes backups before overwriting a matching profile. On Windows the normal Orca config root is %APPDATA%/OrcaSlicer.

The default machine contains only printer-wide requirements: Klipper flavor, START_PRINT/END_PRINT, object labels, exclude objects, by-layer printing, printer-owned power-loss behavior, pause/M600 hooks, zero Z-hop, zero restart extra, and the standard layer timelapse hook. A separate 0.4 mm Collision Clearance machine variant is available for geometry that needs it. Frieren supports and other one-print choices live in process projects, while temperature, flow, pressure advance, maximum volumetric speed, and retraction live in filament profiles after measurement.
What not to put in Orca
No factory corner prime line.
No G28 or BED_MESH commands inside the slice.
No SMART_PARK or LINE_PURGE commands from the slice.
No direct M104, M109, M140, or M190 startup heat sequence from Orca.
No power-loss recovery commands from Orca.
No temporary 125 percent flow experiment as a shared default.
What still needs normal calibration

The migration does not magically tune filament. For each real spool, especially the white PLA and the orange PLA, we still need Orca-supported calibration for temperature, flow ratio, pressure advance, retraction, and maximum volumetric speed. Those are what should improve stringing, surface finish, and clean travel behavior.
Recommended filament calibration order

After reviewing Factorian Designs' Filament Calibration Masterclass and OrcaSlicer's calibration guidance, the practical lesson is: do not use a first-layer sheet or a big flow multiplier to tune a whole spool. First-layer tests are mainly for bed contact, Z offset, mesh behavior, and adhesion. Filament calibration should happen on normal Orca calibration tools and should be saved per filament profile.
First prove the printer-side baseline: Z offset, full mesh at bed temperature, GerGo gantry alignment, and one slow extruder rotation-distance measurement if extrusion amount still looks suspicious.
Then run Orca's temperature calibration for the chosen spool. Temperature affects stringing, gloss, layer bonding, bridging, and how much flow the hotend can actually melt.
Next run maximum volumetric speed so Orca knows the safe melt-rate ceiling for that filament and hotend. This prevents high-speed under-extrusion that can look like bad flow or bad Z.
Then tune pressure advance or Orca flow dynamics, because it changes how starts, stops, corners, and support islands are fed.
After that, tune flow ratio with Orca's flow tests and save it to the filament profile. Do not carry forward the old 125 percent first-layer experiment unless a real calibration proves it is needed.
Finally tune retraction and run a small stringing check. If stringing remains after sane temperature and retraction values, test a fresher or dried spool before blaming the model.
Practical feel during prints

The start should feel less frantic because the slicer is not drawing a long stationary or corner line before the printer has dealt with purge placement. The first layer should be more predictable because the printer creates a fresh full mesh at bed temperature. The end should be easier to clean because the head parks high, when there is safe room.
New firmware setup gate

After the recovery backup is proven and the mainline runtime is commissioned, OrcaSlicer must be re-pointed at the audited T300 mainline profile before we slice real prints. Frieren and the camera bracket should stay as editable Orca projects until the post-migration calibrations are known; then we can regenerate final G-code from Orca-supported settings.
Use only Orca-supported orientation, supports, brim, seam, temperature, retraction, flow, pressure advance, timelapse, and profile settings.

Once the relevant filament profile is calibrated, stage both the orange camera bracket and the Frieren figure: keep the editable 3MFs, export final G-code only from those reviewed projects, and place the accepted exports on the print USB.

Treat the bracket as the first practical functional print after calibration. Treat Frieren as a quality-gated print that waits for the white PLA's temperature, pressure advance, flow, and retraction choices.
Keep the Frieren 3MF/project file editable. Do not hand-edit the STL mesh or final G-code to fix quality issues.
Before the full Frieren print, run a small temperature/retraction/stringing calibration on the same white PLA if stringing remains visible.
If the calibrated white PLA still strings badly, compare against the orange PLA before blaming the firmware or model.
Stringing and PLA moisture

PLA is less moisture-sensitive than nylon, TPU, or many PETG spools, but it can still absorb enough water to string, hiss, pop, become brittle, or leave fuzzy travel hairs. No dryer is not an automatic blocker. First tune temperature, retraction, travel behavior, and support settings; if stringing persists across reasonable settings, drying the spool or testing a fresher spool becomes the clean diagnostic step.
Exact Orca 2.4.2 compatibility

The compatibility review used OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 source commit 8500fcdccaa10b5099ac20d252af3a7c560046f1. Its Klipper writer emits pressure advance as SET_PRESSURE_ADVANCE ADVANCE=value. The five requested calibration tools use bounded heater commands, ordinary speed changes, direct pressure-advance values, per-object flow ratios baked into moving extrusion, and normal retract/recover moves. They do not require uploaded TUNING_TOWER.

Adaptive pressure advance remains disabled. A measured pressure-advance value belongs in the filament profile, not the machine profile. The firmware accepts only finite values from 0 through 0.20 during an admitted print, and it rejects smooth-time changes, alternate extruders, unknown parameters, and out-of-range values.
Staged editable projects

Downloads/T300-Orca-Review-20260805 now contains four editable 3MF projects: a 60 mm standard first-layer test, the camera bracket with the orange PLA calibration-required profile, Frieren at 0.12 mm quality, and a second 0.12 mm Frieren candidate with an easier support-release gap. No final G-code is included.

The bracket baseline uses four walls, 20 percent gyroid infill, 0.20 mm layers, no ironing, and currently no supports. Before export, Prepare and Preview must confirm orientation, the camera screw opening, unsupported overhangs, seams, strength paths, and clearance. The calibrated orange filament profile must be selected first.

The Frieren quality baseline uses 0.12 mm layers, three walls, 12 percent gyroid infill, automatic tree-hybrid supports, a 5 mm brim, no ironing, zero Z-hop, and per-layer timelapse calls. The easier-release candidate changes only the support-release choice for comparison. Final support islands, seam placement, estimated duration, collision risk, and timelapse frame count still require visual approval in Prepare and Preview.

Exact Orca CLI slices of the bracket and both Frieren candidates completed successfully and passed the admission scanner. Those G-code files were validation evidence only and are not shipped. The bracket waits for orange PLA calibration; Frieren waits for its chosen filament calibration and a successful bracket print.
Hull and floor-line warning rule

A localized horizontal line can appear where a broad solid floor or deck becomes a much thinner continuing wall, or where sparse infill abruptly becomes several solid layers. Cooling and contraction in the large connected solid area can pull on the cosmetic outer wall. This is often called a hull line, Benchy hull line, box bulge, or floor line. It is not automatically a Z-axis or hardware fault. Irregular lines throughout the full height remain a separate machine-diagnostic signal.

Factorian Designs' 2025 video The Most Misdiagnosed Print Error was transcribed and checked against its primary sources: OrcaSlicer pull request 8107, Prusa's Benchy hull-line investigation, and Orca's current wall, precision, cooling, and overlap documentation. The important correction is that layer-time view can help locate the transition, but smoothing layer time did not reliably fix it. Orca pull request 8107 was closed after about 30 tests because the line persisted. Better-supported influences are model geometry, solid-material coupling, cooling, material and environment, solid-infill speed and path, wall order, Precise Wall, and wall-overlap values.

For every valuable or large model, review Orca Preview by feature type, flow, and layer time before final export. Warn if a broad floor, shelf, or deck changes abruptly into thin walls, if a large solid region terminates beside a cosmetic wall, or if sparse infill changes sharply to solid layers while the same outer wall continues. The warning is advisory: identify the likely height, explain uncertainty, and recommend a small test section when the full job is long or expensive.

Possible remedies include material-appropriate cooling, slower or differently patterned solid infill, Inner/Outer/Inner wall order, Precise Wall, less wall overlap, or owner-directed CAD decoupling such as a chamfer, fillet, rib, segmented ledge, or thicker wall. None is an automatic default. They can change strength, dimensions, overhang behavior, seams, warping, surface character, or print time. Do not manually edit meshes or final G-code.
Current bracket warning

The orange camera bracket has plausible floor-line geometry because its broad base transitions into upright structure. At Z 1.20 mm, its exact validation paths drop from about 411.5 mm of connected solid extrusion on the preceding layer to 14.9 mm while about 33.1 mm of outer-wall extrusion continues. That is a strong risk signal, not proof that a visible line will occur. The exact Orca 2.4.2 slice also resolves to 25 percent infill/wall and top/bottom wall overlap, Inner/Outer wall order, Precise Wall off, monotonic internal solid infill, and full PLA fan availability. Orca documents roughly 10-15 percent overlap as an accumulation-aware range, but reducing overlap can trade bonding strength for appearance. Nothing has been changed automatically. Review the transition and choose deliberately before export.
Current Frieren assessment

No automatic Frieren change is justified. The figure has many cross-section changes, but curved and irregular exterior surfaces are less likely to display one long straight hull line than a box or tray. Preview should still be checked for unusually broad solid sections and abrupt feature-flow changes. Support release, stringing, seam placement, cooling, and calibrated filament behavior remain the higher-priority quality risks.
Important warning

The reviewed profile is for the mainline runtime path. Do not use it on untouched stock Comgrow firmware unless the matching runtime macros are installed, because stock firmware expects its own older macro contract.
